name: Indian Poker
description: Indian Poker (also known as Blind Man's Bluff) is a unique poker variant where each player holds their card(s) against their forehead facing outward, so they can see all opponents' cards but not their own. Players bet based on what they see others holding, creating a game of deduction and reverse psychology.

history.origins: Indian Poker is a modern variant of Blind Man's Bluff adapted to card play. The name 'Indian Poker' comes from the visual similarity to Native American headdresses when cards are held to the forehead. The game has no actual connection to India or Native American culture - it's simply a descriptive name for the way cards are held.
timeline: Early 20th century: Blind Man's Bluff card games emerge
Mid-20th century: 'Indian Poker' name becomes popular
Late 20th century: Featured in poker game collections and home games
Present day: Popular as a party game and ice-breaker
history.cultural: Despite the name, the game has no cultural connection to India or Native Americans. The name refers only to the visual appearance of players with cards on their foreheads. Some prefer the name 'Blind Man's Bluff' to avoid any potential cultural insensitivity.
history.evolution: The game evolved from the children's game Blind Man's Bluff. The poker betting element was added to create a gambling version. Multiple card variants exist but the single-card version is most common.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the highest card (or convincing others you do) when players showdown, or by being the only player not to fold.
rules.gameplay:
1. Each player is dealt one card face down
2. Without looking at their card, players hold it to their forehead so all other players can see it
3. Players look around at all other players' cards
4. A round of betting occurs (similar to poker)
5. Players can fold, call, or raise based on what they see
6. After betting, remaining players showdown
7. The player with the highest card wins the pot
8. If multiple players tie for highest, they split the pot
keyRules: Players must NOT look at their own card(s)
All players can see all cards except their own
Highest card wins in single-card version
Players may fold if they believe their card is low
Bluffing is based on betting patterns, not card hiding

strategy.basic: Fold if you see many high cards (Aces, Kings, Queens) on other players. Call or raise if you see mostly low cards. Remember that you cannot see your own card.
strategy.intermediate: Consider the number of players - with more players, the chance someone has a high card increases. Use position to your advantage - acting last gives more information. Watch betting patterns for tells.
strategy.advanced: Game theory optimal play involves randomizing between calling and folding in marginal situations. Against skilled opponents, use mixed strategies. Consider pot odds relative to the probability your card is highest based on visible cards.
tips: Don't give away information through your reactions
If you see an Ace, you're probably beaten unless you have one too
With multiple players, be more selective about calling
Use reverse psychology - act strong when weak and vice versa
Remember: everyone knows more about your hand than you do
